source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a weak left leg is learning to use a cane. The nurse teaches him to hold it in the:
options: Right hand, moving it with the left leg
Left hand, moving it with the left leg
Right hand, moving it with the right leg
Left hand, moving it before both legs
questions.rationale: The cane is held on the unaffected side and advanced together with the affected leg to shift weight onto the cane.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Assistive devices (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: The client must hold cane on the unaffected hand or side. The cane and the affected leg are advanced together.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on crutches with a casted right leg is going up the stairs. The nurse tells her to step up first with the:
questions.rationale: "Up with the good, down with the bad": the unaffected leg leads going up; the affected leg and crutches lead going down.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Crutch walking (PDF p. 396)
questions.quote: When going up the stairs, advance the "good leg" (unaffected leg) first, followed by the "bad leg" and the crutches.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client may bear little or no weight on the affected leg after knee replacement. Which crutch gait fits?
questions.rationale: In the three-point gait, both crutches and the affected leg advance together, then the unaffected leg.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Crutch walking (PDF p. 396)
questions.quote: Little or no weight — bearing is allowed, e.g. after total hip replacement or total knee replacement.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When walking with crutches, the client should bear his weight on the:
questions.rationale: Weight on the palms prevents pressure on the axillary nerves (crutch palsy).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: the client bears the weight of the body on the palms of the hands, not on the axillae to prevent crutch palsy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in a leg cast is taught quadriceps setting. The purpose of this exercise is to:
options: Keep thigh strength and prevent clots
questions.rationale: Quadriceps setting is isometric: no joint movement, but it maintains thigh strength for crutch walking and helps prevent thrombophlebitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Isometric exercise (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: It strengthens the thigh muscles in preparation for ambulation and crutch — walking gait. It also prevents thrombophlebitis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in a new body (spica) cast has repeated vomiting, bloating and vague abdominal pain. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Cast syndrome in a body cast causes bloating, prolonged nausea, vomiting and distention; windowing may relieve it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Cast care (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: Cast syndrome may occur if the client has body cast. It is manifested by bloated feeling, prolonged nausea, repeated vomiting, abdominal distention

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding distal to a new arm cast shows the cast may be too tight?
questions.rationale: Pallor, coldness, numbness, tingling, inability to move and absent pulse distal to the cast mean impaired circulation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Neurovascular checks (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: Skin temperature — cold skin • Sensation numbness, tingling

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in Buck's traction for a hip fracture asks if the weights can rest on the floor at night. The nurse explains the weights must:
options: Rest on the floor while asleep
questions.rationale: Traction must be continuous with weights hanging freely; there should be no knots or friction along the rope.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Traction principles (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: Allow the weights to hang freely. Weights should not touch the floor.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An 18-month-old in Bryant traction for a femur fracture is positioned correctly when the:
options: Buttocks are slightly off the mattress
Buttocks rest flat on the bed
Legs are flat on the bed
questions.rationale: In Bryant traction both legs are at 90 degrees with buttocks slightly raised so body weight gives countertraction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Bryant traction (PDF p. 398)
questions.quote: Buttocks must be slightly off the mattress. To enhance efficiency of the weight as countertraction.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has a skeletal traction pin with redness, warmth and pus at the site. The nurse should:
options: Cover it and recheck in a week
questions.rationale: Pin sites are cleaned as ordered and observed for infection; redness, swelling, warmth and drainage are reported.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Pin site care (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: Observe site for signs and symptoms of infection, e.g., redness, swelling, pain, warmth, drainage. Notify physician

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A basketball player twisted his ankle 1 hour ago. It is swollen and painful. The nurse first applies:
questions.rationale: RICE limits edema and pain after a sprain; heat and massage increase swelling early.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Strain and sprain (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: R— est / immobilize affected joint I — ce application

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A child fell from a tree. X-ray shows one side of the forearm bone broken and the other side bent. This is a:
questions.rationale: Greenstick fractures are incomplete: one side breaks, the other bends; common in children's flexible bones.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Types of fracture (PDF p. 400)
questions.quote: Greenstick. One side of the bone is impaired, the other side is bent.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An elderly woman fell at home. Which finding suggests hip fracture?
questions.rationale: Muscle spasm shortens the limb; adduction and external rotation of the hip are typical deformities.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Fracture manifestations (PDF p. 400)
questions.quote: Obvious deformity, e.g. adduction and external rotation of the hip in hip fracture.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A day after a femur fracture, a client becomes confused and short of breath, with petechiae on the chest. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Fat embolism follows long-bone or multiple fractures and may lead to ARDS; it is an emergency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Complications of fractures (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Fat Embolism. This usually follows fracture of the long bones, e.g. lower extremities or multiple fractures. It may lead to acute respiratory distress

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a tibia fracture in a cast has severe pain not relieved by analgesics and tingling toes. The nurse should first:
options: Elevate the leg high on pillows
questions.rationale: These suggest compartment syndrome, which can cause ischemia and necrosis; report at once and loosen tight dressings or cast as ordered. Keep the limb at heart level.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Compartment syndrome (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Notify physician. Compartment syndrome may cause tissue ischemia and necrosis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which complication of a hip fracture results from loss of blood supply to the femoral head?
questions.rationale: Decreased perfusion causes bone death; the neck and head of the femur are commonly affected.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Complications of fractures (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Avascular Necrosis. Decreased bone tissue perfusion leads to bone tissue death. Neck of the femur is commonly affected.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After hip replacement, a client's operated leg keeps rolling outward in bed. The nurse places a:
questions.rationale: Trochanter rolls along the hip prevent external rotation, which can dislocate the prosthesis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Total hip replacement (PDF p. 402)
questions.quote: Prevent extemal rotation by placing trochanter rolls along hip.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After an above-knee amputation, which position helps prevent a hip flexion contracture?
options: Stump on a pillow all day
Sitting in a chair for hours
questions.rationale: Lying prone with the hip extended prevents flexion contracture; avoid long sitting, pillows under the stump after 24 hours, and abduction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Amputation (PDF p. 414)
questions.quote: Have patient assume prone position several times a day and position hip in extension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has painful, swollen finger joints on both hands, stiff for over an hour each morning. This suggests:
questions.rationale: RA is autoimmune and symmetrical, affects small joints of the hands, and causes morning stiffness.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Rheumatoid arthritis (PDF p. 403)
questions.quote: Joint distribution is symmetrical (both sides of the body are affected) — most commonly affects smaller peripheral joints of hands

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To ease morning stiffness, a client with rheumatoid arthritis is advised to:
options: Take a warm bath or shower
questions.rationale: Warm baths in the morning relieve stiffness; cold is for acute pain, then heat.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 RA management (PDF p. 404)
questions.quote: Warm bath in the morning. To relieve morning stiffness.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with long-standing RA has dry eyes, dry mouth and vaginal dryness. This is:
questions.rationale: Sjögren's syndrome causes excessive dryness of eyes, mouth and vagina; Felty's is leukopenia with splenomegaly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 RA complications (PDF p. 404)
questions.quote: Sjoren's syndrome is characterized by: Excessive dryness of the eyes, mouth and vagina.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An obese 68-year-old has knee pain that worsens with walking and eases with rest, with bony nodes at the finger tips. This suggests:
questions.rationale: OA is degenerative, affects weight-bearing joints, worsens with use, and causes Heberden's nodes at distal joints.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteoarthritis (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: Pain aggravated by use and relieved by rest.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A man wakes with a red, hot, very painful big toe after a party with beer and organ meats. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Gout is a disorder of purine metabolism with urate crystals; the big toe is most often affected, and alcohol and purine-rich foods trigger attacks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Gout (PDF p. 405)
questions.quote: Joint pain, redness, heat, swelling; great/ big toe and ankle are most commonly affected.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client starting allopurinol for gout should be taught to:
questions.rationale: High fluid intake prevents uric acid kidney stones; aspirin can trigger attacks; sardines and organ meats are high in purine.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Antigout medications (PDF p. 406)
questions.quote: Maintain a fluid intake ofat least 2000 to 3000 ml. a day to avoid kidney stones.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does allopurinol work in gout?
questions.rationale: Allopurinol inhibits uric acid formation; probenecid increases urinary excretion; colchicine or NSAIDs treat acute attacks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Gout drugs (PDF p. 406)
questions.quote: Zyloprim (Allopurinol) inhibits uric acid formation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A young woman with SLE has a rash over the nose and cheeks. The nurse teaches her to:
questions.rationale: Sun exposure triggers SLE flares; use sunscreen, long sleeves, hats and sunglasses.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 SLE (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: Avoid exposure to sunlight. To prevent exacerbation of manifestations.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which laboratory test is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.rationale: Anti-double-stranded DNA is the most specific; ESR only shows inflammation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 SLE diagnostics (PDF p. 408)
questions.quote: Anti - DNA (most specific)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Osteomyelitis after an open fracture is most often caused by:
questions.rationale: S. aureus is the most common cause; infection enters through wounds, blood or nearby tissue.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Osteomyelitis (PDF p. 409)
questions.quote: most commonly caused by Staphylococcus Aureus.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has low back pain radiating down the leg. Raising the straight leg causes pain below the knee. This suggests:
questions.rationale: A positive straight leg raise (Lasègue's sign) indicates nerve root compression, most often L4–L5.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 HNP (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: Positive straight leg raise test; pain on leg below the knee when leg raised from a supine position (Lasegue's sign).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a lumbar laminectomy, how should the nurse turn the client?
options: Have him twist to his side
Pull him up by the arms
Bend his knees to his chest
questions.rationale: Log rolling keeps the spine aligned; a pillow under the head and between the legs reduces strain.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Laminectomy (PDF p. 411)
questions.quote: Use log rolling technique or Stryker frame.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cervical spine surgery, which equipment should be at the bedside?
questions.rationale: Neck edema may impair swallowing and breathing; assess airway and keep suction and a tracheostomy set ready.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 11 Laminectomy (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: With cervical spinal surgery: assess swallowing, coughing; check for respiratory distress; have suction and tracheostomy set at bedside.
